**sigmoid**: the function $\sigma(z) = 1/(1 + e^{-z})$ that maps any real number to $(0, 1)$ and is the inverse of the logit; its slope is $\sigma(1 - \sigma)$, at most $1/4$. *([Classification and Logistic Regression](v02-learning/03-logistic-regression.md))*

**silu**: the sigmoid linear unit $z\,\sigma(z)$ (also called swish), the input times the logistic sigmoid of the input, smooth, with a slope that overshoots $1$ before settling to it. *([Multilayer Networks](v03-neural-networks/02-mlp.md))*

**SIMD**: single instruction, multiple data: an instruction that applies the same operation to all the lanes of a wide register at once, for example eight f32 additions in one 256-bit instruction. *([The CPU: Cores, Caches and Vectors](v04-computation/02-cpu.md))*

**SIMT execution**: single instruction, multiple threads: the hardware issues each instruction once for a fixed group of threads, each applying it to its own registers, so a program is written for one thread and the group's lanes are filled by the hardware. *([The GPU: Thousands of Small Workers](v04-computation/04-gpu.md))*

**singular value decomposition**: the factorisation $\mathbf{A} = \mathbf{U}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}\mathbf{V}^\top$ of any matrix into a rotation, a stretch by non-negative singular values and a second rotation. *([Eigenvalues, Rotations and Low-Rank Structure](v01-mathematics/06-decompositions.md))*

**sinusoid**: a wave $A\cos(2\pi f t + \varphi)$ described by an amplitude $A$ (its largest value), a frequency $f$ (cycles per second) and a phase $\varphi$ (where in its cycle it stands at time zero); a cosine and a sine are the same sinusoid a quarter period apart. *([Complex Numbers, Frequencies and the Fourier Transform](v01-mathematics/14-fourier.md))*

**softmax**: the function that turns a vector of real scores into a probability vector by exponentiating each score and dividing by the sum of the exponentials, so that the outputs are positive, add to one and keep the order of the scores. *([Softmax, Logits and Cross-Entropy](v03-neural-networks/03-softmax.md))*

**softmax-cross-entropy**: the loss of a classifier computed directly from its scores and the true class as the log-sum-exp of the scores minus the score of the true class; it is the negative log-likelihood of the true class under the softmax, and its gradient with respect to the scores is the probability vector minus the one-hot target. *([Softmax, Logits and Cross-Entropy](v03-neural-networks/03-softmax.md))*

**sorting**: rearranging a list into non-decreasing order; comparison sorts need $\Omega(n \log n)$ comparisons in the worst case and merge sort achieves it, while sorts that use the values of integer keys as addresses can be linear. *([Algorithms, Cost and Complexity](v01-mathematics/16-algorithms.md))*

**stable-softmax**: the softmax computed after subtracting the largest score from every score, which gives the same probabilities but keeps every exponent at most zero, so nothing overflows and the sum is at least one. *([Softmax, Logits and Cross-Entropy](v03-neural-networks/03-softmax.md))*

**standard error**: the standard deviation of an estimator over repeated samples, the typical size of its error; for the sample mean it is $\sigma/\sqrt{n}$, estimated by $s/\sqrt{n}$. *([Statistics: Learning Facts from Samples](v01-mathematics/12-statistics.md))*

**stochastic gradient descent**: gradient descent that steps along the gradient of a small random batch of examples instead of the whole training set, $\theta \leftarrow \theta - \eta\,\mathbf{g}_t$, an unbiased but noisy estimate of the full step. *([Optimizers: From SGD to AdamW](v03-neural-networks/07-optimizers.md))*

**storage buffer**: a large array in device memory that a kernel reads or reads and writes, whose element type the kernel declares and whose length the host chooses when it binds the buffer. *([Writing Compute Kernels](v04-computation/05-compute-kernels.md))*

**stride**: the distance in memory, counted in elements, between two neighbours along one axis; a view is described by one stride per axis, and stride 0 repeats one number. *([Arrays, Shapes, Strides and Broadcasting](v01-mathematics/05-arrays.md))*

**subgroup**: the group of consecutive invocations of a workgroup, 32 in this book's model, that the hardware executes with one instruction at a time. *([The GPU: Thousands of Small Workers](v04-computation/04-gpu.md))*

**summation notation**: the symbol $\sum_{i=a}^{b} x_i$ for the sum of the terms $x_i$ as the index $i$ runs from $a$ to $b$. *([Numbers, Quantities and Notation](v01-mathematics/01-numbers.md))*

**supervised learning**: learning from examples that all carry labels, in order to predict the label of a new example. *([The Learning Problem](v02-learning/01-learning-problem.md))*

**symmetry-breaking**: starting the units of a layer with different weights, by random draws, so that their gradients differ; units that start identical stay identical forever. *([Initialization: Where Training Starts](v03-neural-networks/09-initialization.md))*

## T

**tanh-activation**: the hyperbolic tangent used as a neuron's activation, a smooth step from $-1$ to $1$ equal to $2\sigma(2z) - 1$ with slope $1 - \tanh^2(z)$, centred on zero and saturating for large $|z|$. *([Multilayer Networks](v03-neural-networks/02-mlp.md))*

**Taylor expansion**: the polynomial that matches a function's value and first derivatives at a point, such as $f(a) + f'(a)h + \tfrac{1}{2}f''(a)h^2$, whose error is of the order of the first term dropped. *([Gradients, Jacobians and Many Variables](v01-mathematics/08-multivariable-calculus.md))*

**tensor**: an array of numbers with any number of axes (zero for a scalar, one for a vector, two for a matrix), described by its shape. *([Arrays, Shapes, Strides and Broadcasting](v01-mathematics/05-arrays.md))*

**tensor core**: a hardware unit that multiplies two small fixed-size matrices and adds a third in one operation, usually with narrow inputs and a wider accumulator, raising the peak arithmetic rate of a device for matrix products. *([Making Matrix Multiplication Fast](v04-computation/06-matmul.md))*

**test set**: rows used once, after every choice is made, to report the final score of the chosen model; looking at it more than once turns it into a validation set. *([Generalization, Overfitting and Honest Evaluation](v02-learning/05-generalization.md))*

**test-dimension choice**: choosing the sizes of the model a test runs on (batch, features, widths, heads) all different and above 1, so that bugs that confuse two sizes or depend on a size of 1 change the result. *([Proving Gradients Correct](v03-neural-networks/06-gradient-checking.md))*

**thread parallelism**: using several threads, each running on its own core with its own registers and first caches and sharing the later caches and memory, to carry out the pieces of one computation at the same time. *([The CPU: Cores, Caches and Vectors](v04-computation/02-cpu.md))*

**tiled matmul**: the matrix product computed one tile of the output at a time, with the matching tiles of the two inputs staged in a fast memory so that each number loaded is used once per row or column of the tile, cutting the loads from $2n^3$ to $2n^3/T$ for a tile of side $T$. *([Making Matrix Multiplication Fast](v04-computation/06-matmul.md))*

**train-vs-eval-mode**: the two behaviours of a layer that has a state of its own: in train mode batch normalization uses the batch statistics and updates its running averages, in eval mode it uses the running averages and changes nothing. *([Normalization Layers](v03-neural-networks/10-normalization.md))*

**training set**: the rows used to fit a model's parameters, and no other decisions; the error on it is a flattering estimate of the error on new rows. *([Generalization, Overfitting and Honest Evaluation](v02-learning/05-generalization.md))*

**transpose**: the matrix $\mathbf{A}^\top$ with rows and columns swapped; $(\mathbf{A}\mathbf{B})^\top = \mathbf{B}^\top\mathbf{A}^\top$. *([Matrices as Linear Maps](v01-mathematics/04-matrices.md))*

**tree reduction**: a parallel reduction that combines the values in pairs, then the pairs in pairs, so that $n$ values need $n - 1$ combinations in only $\lceil \log_2 n \rceil$ dependent steps; inside a workgroup it is a loop over strides with a barrier after each step. *([Parallel Reductions, Scans and Sorting](v04-computation/07-reductions.md))*

**two's complement**: the representation of negative whole numbers in which the pattern of $-x$ is $2^n - x$ (the bits of $x$ inverted, plus one), so that the same addition works for both signs, the top bit is the sign, and the range is $-2^{n-1} \dots 2^{n-1} - 1$. *([Bits and Number Formats](v04-computation/01-number-formats.md))*

**two-pass reduction**: the reduction of an array longer than a workgroup by two dispatches, one in which every workgroup writes a partial result for its slice and a second that reduces the partials, the end of the first dispatch serving as the barrier between workgroups that a dispatch cannot have. *([Parallel Reductions, Scans and Sorting](v04-computation/07-reductions.md))*

## U

**underfitting**: a model too restricted to represent the pattern, so that its error is high on the training rows and on new rows alike. *([Generalization, Overfitting and Honest Evaluation](v02-learning/05-generalization.md))*

**Unicode**: the standard that numbers every character of every writing system once (its code point, from U+0000 to U+10FFFF) and records its properties, such as category, combining class and case. *([Text as Data](v05-sequences/01-text.md))*

**uniform parameters**: the small block of constants, the same for every invocation and read-only, that the host writes into a separate buffer for a kernel: element counts, scalars, shapes and strides. *([Writing Compute Kernels](v04-computation/05-compute-kernels.md))*

**universal-approximation**: the theorem that, for any continuous function on a closed bounded set and any tolerance, some one-hidden-layer network with a non-polynomial activation stays within that tolerance everywhere on the set; it guarantees that the weights exist, not how many units they need or how to find them. *([Multilayer Networks](v03-neural-networks/02-mlp.md))*

**unsupervised learning**: learning from examples without labels, to find structure such as groups in the features themselves. *([The Learning Problem](v02-learning/01-learning-problem.md))*

**UTF-8**: the encoding that writes each Unicode scalar value as 1 to 4 bytes whose leading bits announce the sequence's length, compatible with ASCII, self-synchronizing and ordered like the code points; its decoder is a state machine of eight states. *([Text as Data](v05-sequences/01-text.md))*

## V

**validation set**: rows kept apart from fitting and used to choose between models (degree, penalty, learning rate, when to stop); the score of the chosen model on it is optimistic, because it was chosen for its score. *([Generalization, Overfitting and Honest Evaluation](v02-learning/05-generalization.md))*

**vanishing-gradient**: the gradient reaching the early layers of a deep network is a tiny fraction of the one at the top, because it is a product of layer Jacobians whose factors are below one; those layers do not learn. *([Training Dynamics and Debugging](v03-neural-networks/12-training-dynamics.md))*

**variance**: the expected squared deviation from the mean, $\mathbb{E}[X^2] - \mathbb{E}[X]^2$, which scales by $a^2$ under multiplication by $a$ and adds over independent variables; its square root is the standard deviation. *([Probability: Reasoning Under Uncertainty](v01-mathematics/10-probability.md))*

**variance-preservation**: choosing the scale of the weights so that the typical size of activations (and of gradients) is the same in every layer, neither shrinking nor growing with depth. *([Initialization: Where Training Starts](v03-neural-networks/09-initialization.md))*

**vector**: an ordered list of real numbers, read as data (the features of one example) or as an arrow with a length and a direction. *([Vectors: Lists of Numbers with Geometry](v01-mathematics/03-vectors.md))*

**vector addition**: adding two vectors of the same length entry by entry; as arrows it is the parallelogram rule. *([Vectors: Lists of Numbers with Geometry](v01-mathematics/03-vectors.md))*

**vector-Jacobian product**: the product of a row vector with a Jacobian, computed by a per-operation rule without ever building the Jacobian as a matrix. *([Backpropagation Derived from Scratch](v03-neural-networks/04-backpropagation.md))*

## W

**warmup runs**: the leading runs of a repeated measurement whose cost is dominated by a start-up transient (building pipelines, first-touch memory, cold caches, a clock that has not ramped up) and is not the cost of the steady state; they are detected and kept out of the summary, or reported as a separate cold row. *([Measuring Performance Honestly](v04-computation/11-profiling.md))*

**weight decay**: shrinking every weight toward zero by the fraction $\eta\lambda$ at each step, as a regularizer of a neural network; the L2 penalty of Volume II, applied directly to the weights in the decoupled form of chapter 7. *([Regularization in Neural Networks](v03-neural-networks/11-regularization.md))*

**weight-only quantization**: storing the weights as low-bit codes with scales while the activations stay in a higher-precision format, decoding the codes inside the matrix product so that the bytes read, and not the arithmetic, shrink. *([Quantization: Fewer Bits per Weight](v04-computation/12-quantization.md))*

**WGSL**: the WebGPU Shading Language, a small kernel language that compiles to the native graphics interfaces and in which the book writes its kernel examples. *([Writing Compute Kernels](v04-computation/05-compute-kernels.md))*

**whole-pass measurement**: the time of the whole unit of work a user waits for, with every dispatch, wait, copy and host-side step the real use performs inside the bracket, repeated and summarized with its spread; the number by which a change is judged. *([Measuring Performance Honestly](v04-computation/11-profiling.md))*

**workgroup**: a set of invocations of one dispatch that run together on one compute unit, share an on-chip memory and can wait for each other at a barrier, while different workgroups are independent. *([The GPU: Thousands of Small Workers](v04-computation/04-gpu.md))*

## X

**xavier-initialization**: drawing the weights of a layer with variance $2/(n_{\mathrm{in}} + n_{\mathrm{out}})$, the harmonic mean of the forward-preserving and backward-preserving variances, for units that behave like the identity near zero. *([Initialization: Where Training Starts](v03-neural-networks/09-initialization.md))*

**XOR problem**: the fact that the exclusive-or of two bits, whose two classes sit on opposite diagonals of a square, is not linearly separable and so no single threshold neuron computes it. *([The Neuron and the Perceptron](v03-neural-networks/01-perceptron.md))*
